title: Education Sector Displacement by 2030
description: Projected percentage of education roles (tutoring, grading, content creation, administration) restructured or reduced by AI by 2030. AI adoption is high (92% of students, 60% of teachers use AI tools) but studies consistently frame AI as augmenting educators, not displacing them. The 33,000 higher ed jobs cut in 2025 (BLS) were driven by federal funding policy, not AI. SHRM found education has the lowest automation rate of any sector at 7.3%. Direct AI-specific displacement estimates remain unusually sparse.
disclaimer: Insufficient evidence for confident projection. Only 4 data points, two of which are corporate proxies (Chegg, Pearson) rather than sector-wide measurements. BLS projects just 3% displacement in education support roles, and SHRM found education has the lowest automation rate of any sector at 7.3%. Treat this estimate with more caution than others on this site.

sources.title: Guidance for Generative AI in Education and Research
sources.excerpt: AI tutoring systems can handle 60% of routine student queries. Teaching assistants and tutors face the most immediate displacement risk.

sources.title: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools in K-12 Classrooms
sources.excerpt: Surveyed 1,020 teachers nationally; 18% of K-12 teachers used AI for teaching with most using adaptive learning systems weekly. 60% of districts planned to train teachers on AI.

sources.title: Professor tailored AI tutor to physics course. Engagement doubled.
sources.excerpt: Learning gains for students in the AI-tutored group were about double those for the in-class group. Students using the AI tutor reported significantly more engagement and motivation to learn.

sources.title: Chegg Q2 2024 Earnings — ChatGPT Impact on Tutoring Market
sources.excerpt: Chegg subscribers fell 50% from peak as students shifted to ChatGPT. Company laid off 23% of workforce, citing AI as primary competitive threat.

sources.title: Are You Ready for the AI University?
sources.excerpt: Over the next decade AI will decimate faculty ranks; TAs will be first casualties, then non-tenured faculty, then tenured positions via attrition. Predicts significant culling of doctoral programs.

sources.title: OECD Education at a Glance 2025: AI and Teaching
sources.excerpt: Teaching roles are among the least automatable (15% task exposure), but education support staff, administration, and tutoring face 30-40% task displacement. Blended estimate across the full education workforce: ~20%.

sources.title: Occupational Outlook: Education, Training, and Library
sources.excerpt: Teacher aide and educational support employment projected to decline 3%. Post-secondary teacher demand flat. Private tutoring category declining.

sources.title: Pearson plc 2024 Annual Report — AI Strategy
sources.excerpt: Pearson pivoted to AI-first content delivery, reducing editorial headcount by 18% while growing AI-generated adaptive learning content 300%.

sources.title: Future of Jobs Report 2025: Education Sector Analysis
sources.excerpt: Education support roles face moderate displacement risk while core teaching remains protected. Administrative and content creation roles most affected by AI adoption.

sources.title: Generative AI and the future of work in America
sources.excerpt: An additional 12 million occupational shifts expected by 2030. Workers in lower-wage jobs are up to 14 times more likely to need to change occupations. Activities accounting for up to 30% of hours could be automated.

sources.title: Bridging Skill Gaps for the Future: New Jobs Creation in the AI Age
sources.excerpt: Around 40% of global employment is exposed to AI; in advanced economies 60%. Demand for new skills is rising with 10% of jobs in advanced economies requiring at least one new skill.

sources.title: Chegg Eliminates 636 Employees in Two Rounds of AI-Driven Layoffs
sources.excerpt: Chegg eliminated 636 employees across two rounds of layoffs (23% in 2024, then additional cuts in early 2025), totaling ~67% of peak workforce. CEO explicitly cited AI as existential threat to homework-help business model.

sources.title: Duolingo Cuts Contractors as AI Replaces Content Creation
sources.excerpt: Duolingo cut 10%+ of its contractor workforce, explicitly replacing human content creators with AI-generated language exercises. CEO announced 'AI-first' strategy for all content production.

sources.title: Automation, Generative AI, and Job Displacement Risk in U.S. Employment
sources.excerpt: At least 50% of tasks are automated in only 7.3% of education and library occupations — the lowest of any occupational group. Survey of 20,262 U.S. workers fielded March-April 2025.

sources.title: The Impact of AI on Work in Higher Education
sources.excerpt: 94% of higher education workers use AI tools for work, but only 54% are aware of institutional AI policies. 67% identified six or more urgent AI-related risks, including job loss. Survey of 1,960 staff and faculty across 1,800+ institutions.

sources.title: New Work, New World 2026: How AI is Reshaping Work
sources.excerpt: Education task exposure jumped from 11% to 49% — a 4.5x increase driven by multimodal AI, advanced reasoning, and agentic systems. Based on reassessment of 18,000 tasks across 1,000 O*NET occupations.

sources.title: How AI Impacts Skill Formation
sources.excerpt: AI use impairs conceptual understanding, code reading, and debugging abilities. The AI group averaged 50% on the quiz, compared to 67% in the hand-coding group. The AI didn't make developers faster on average.

sources.title: Ellucian's 3rd Annual Higher Education AI Survey
sources.excerpt: The survey shows institutional adoption is accelerating, with 66% of respondents reporting their institution is currently leveraging AI, an increase from 49% year over year. Eighty-eight percent of respondents say they expect institutional AI use to increase over the next two years. Survey of 779 higher education faculty and administrators from 300+ institutions.

sources.title: Predictions for AI's Next 20 Years by the US Public and AI Experts
sources.excerpt: 31% of AI experts predict AI will lead to fewer teacher jobs in 20 years, vs 43% of general public. Survey of 1,013 AI experts (Aug-Oct 2024) and 5,410 US adults. AI experts far more optimistic: 73% say positive impact on jobs vs 23% of public.

sources.title: Does Generative AI Narrow Education-Based Productivity Gaps? Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
sources.publisher: NBER (Cruces, Fernández Meijide, Galiani, Gálvez, Lombardi)
sources.excerpt: In a randomized experiment with 1,174 adults ages 25-45, AI access closed approximately three-quarters of the education-based productivity gap: higher-education participants outperform lower-education participants by 0.548 standard deviations without AI; with AI, this gap falls to 0.139 standard deviations.

sources.title: PwC 2025 Global AI Jobs Barometer
sources.excerpt: In job postings in the US, those professions most exposed to AI have seen a 55% greater change in skills requested by employers.

sources.title: Will Wired Belts Become the New Rust Belts? AI and the Emerging Geography of American Job Risk
sources.publisher: Digital Planet, The Fletcher School, Tufts University
sources.excerpt: Educational Services 8.3%
